newsitem.title: USA: Alabama $700 million highway bond plan fails.
newsitem.headline: Alabama $700 million highway bond plan fails.

text.p: Gov. Fob James' $700 million highway bond proposal failed in the legislature, a James spokeswoman said Tuesday.
The proposal passed in the House but stalled in the Senate, where it failed to reach the floor before lawmakers adjourned ahead of a midnight deadline Monday night.

The proposal would have been the largest state bond issue in Alabama history. It would have used current gasoline taxes to pay debt service on the bonds, with proceeds used to build urban bypasses, repair bridges, repave local roads and widen two-lane highways.
The legislature could reconsider the plan in a special session, but James has not yet decided whether to call one, his spokeswoman said.
Lawmakers also approved a $1 billion general fund budget and a $3 billion public education budget during the final hours of the session.
